ConnectionAuthorityModel.description: The authority interpretation fixed by a connection type.

ConnectionField.description: A field whose ownership is fixed by a connection-type descriptor.

ConnectionFieldOwner.description: The principal allowed to supply one connection field.

ConnectionFieldOwnership.description: Canonical ownership for one connection field.

ConnectionTypeDescriptor.description: Versioned portable semantics for one connection type.

CredentialInjection.description: How environment-owned credentials enter a request.

CredentialRef.description: A credential the flow references by logical name; the vault (5.9) resolves it to a lazy handle at run time. No secret material is ever stored in flow data.

kind.description: Optional hint for the editor's credential picker (e.g. `http-basic`, `api-key`).

Edge.description: A wire from one node's output port to a downstream node. Branch = several edges from distinct ports of one node; merge = several edges into one node.

from-port.description: Source output port. Defaults to [`MAIN_PORT`]; [`ERROR_PORT`] is the error path; node-library node types may define others (e.g. a `conditional`'s `true`/`false`).

ordinal.description:
This edge's **fan-out order** within its `(from, from-port)` group: the sequence the engine dispatches a branch's targets in ([`crate::Flow`] consumers see it through `Plan::successors`).

Fan-out order is author-meaningful and therefore an explicit value, never an element's position in the `edges` array (W2 digest ordering rule 2). An authored document may omit it; [`Flow::from_json`] then materializes the edge's position within its group exactly once, at parse, so the document's order is preserved as an explicit value and array position stops mattering thereafter. Only order *within* a group is meaningful: two edges leaving different nodes or different ports never compare.

`None` therefore only appears on a flow built in Rust without going through [`Flow::from_json`]; it sorts as `0`, which for such a flow keeps the array order it was built in.

to-port.description: Target input port. Defaults to the node's single input; present only for future multi-input node types.

FlowConnectionRequirement.description: One artifact-local name bound to a portable connection requirement.

requirement.description: Portable type, contract, and field-ownership requirement.

config.description: Opaque per-node configuration — a JSON object typed by the node library (5.3), not by this crate.

connection.description: The artifact-local connection requirement consumed by this integrate node. Pure and control nodes do not carry a connection.

credential.description: Optional reference to a declared credential by [`CredentialRef::name`].

type.description: The node type. Engine-reserved types are checked here; ordinary open strings are resolved through the pinned public node interfaces.

Ordering.description:
The flow's record-stream **ordering** (5.11): which ordered stream a run joins. This is the run's `run_queue.partition_key` seam — the dispatcher evaluates the declaration at fire() and stamps the key; a NULL key is the order-agnostic global claim. Orthogonal to [`PartitionPolicy`], which ranks runs *within* one stream (D20). Absent = [`Ordering::Unordered`].

Per-node ordering (the 5.11 plan wording) is deferred: the queue's dispatch unit is the **run** (records map 1:1 to runs, D9), so ordering is declared on the flow, not per node — a later refinement if per-node streams are ever needed. See `docs/archive/execution/run-queue.md` §Flow-level ordering declaration.

oneOf.description: No ordering: runs dispatch by the global claim in `available_at` order (`partition_key` NULL). Today's behavior, and the default.
The whole flow is ONE ordered stream: every run carries a constant partition key (the flow id), so the flow's runs dispatch strictly in-order — one in flight per stream — across replicas.

Per-key ordering: the run's partition key is a [JMESPath] over the run input. Runs sharing a key dispatch in-order; distinct keys dispatch independently.

[JMESPath]: https://jmespath.org/

partition-key.description: The JMESPath expression evaluated over the run input to produce the stream key. Validated for syntactic well-formedness by [`crate::validate`].

PartitionPolicy.description: The `partitioned(key)` head-unavailability policy (5.11 / D20): what a key does while its earliest (head) run cannot dispatch. The stream order the policy ranks by is `(enqueued_at, run_id)` — stamped once at enqueue, never moved by a park/backoff (unlike `available_at`).

oneOf.description: The default: an unavailable head still **blocks** its key — a backed-off or parked head holds later runs until it completes, and a head that exhausts its redelivery budget **wedges** the key (operator release; the janitor's `infrastructure-failure` verdict does not free it). The Kafka-consumer model: a partition never leapfrogs.

Opt-in: a later ready run may overtake an unavailable head (the `(available_at, run_id)` order among currently-ready siblings), and the janitor's verdict on an exhausted head releases the key. For keys where ordering is a throughput heuristic, not a correctness requirement.

description: One version of a flow — the unit stored in the catalog and pointed at by the active-version pointer (deploying = flipping that pointer + a NATS doorbell, 5.14).

allowed-hosts.description: Hosts this flow's outbound HTTP may reach (fqg.11). Entries use the host allowlist grammar: `host[:port]`, `scheme://host[:port]`, or a `*.suffix` subdomain wildcard. Egress is opt-in and fail-closed — undeclared (or empty) means DENY-ALL for the flow, and a declared host is still bounded by the runner's host-level allowlist (both must allow). Mirrors [`Flow::credentials`]: capability by declaration.

connection-requirements.description: Portable connection requirements named by this artifact. Environment bindings, instances, generations, authorities, and secrets never enter this declaration or the artifact identity derived from it.

credentials.description: Credentials the flow needs, declared by logical name and resolved by the vault (5.9) at run time. Nodes reference these by [`Node::credential`]; secrets never appear in flow data.

edges.description: The wiring between node output ports and downstream nodes.

flow-id.description: Stable identifier shared across every version of this flow.

nodes.description: The nodes of the graph. Exactly one has a type in [`ENTRY_TYPES`].

ordering.description: The flow's record-stream ordering (5.11): which ordered stream its runs join. Absent = [`Ordering::Unordered`] (today's global-claim behavior). The dispatcher evaluates this at fire() and stamps `run_queue.partition_key` ([`Ordering::partition_key_for`]); the CDC materializer (wamn-l5i9.17) consumes the SAME declaration. Composes with [`Flow::partition_policy`], which is the head-unavailability policy *within* a stream (orthogonal: this picks the stream, that ranks it).

partition-policy.description: How this flow's `partitioned(key)` runs dispatch when the key's earliest (head) run is unavailable — backed off, parked, or budget-exhausted (5.11 ordering decision, D20). Absent = [`PartitionPolicy::Blocking`]: choosing partitioned dispatch *is* opting into ordering. Inert for a flow whose runs carry no partition key; materialized onto each queue row at enqueue (`wamn-run-state`) so the claim SQL is self-contained.
